items.text: Votes to keep in place the existing system, in which public health coverage is guaranteed to older, disabled, and low-income residents, most others rely on employer or subsidized private insurance, and about 8 percent of residents have no coverage.

Votes to keep in place the existing income support, in which mandatory pension schemes replace about 51 percent of an average worker's net earnings and a single adult with no other income is guaranteed about 6 percent of the median income.

At a rally in a district held by the majority party, criticized the local legislator for voting for a budget plan that an official analysis found would require reductions in public health coverage for low-income residents.
Cosponsored a bill to enroll every resident in a single public health plan covering medical, dental, vision, hearing, mental health, and long-term care, with no premiums, deductibles, or copayments.
